headline: Clinton order set up a national commission and a presidential council to study "offsets" in defense and commercial trade.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order created two groups. One is a National Commission to look at offsets in defense trade. Offsets are deals where a country buying US goods, such as military equipment, requires the seller to give something back, like local jobs or investment. The other is a President's Council to look at offsets in commercial, or non-military, trade.

who_it_affects.group: US defense contractors that sell to foreign governments
who_it_affects.how: Their use of offset deals in foreign sales was set to be studied by the new national commission.

who_it_affects.group: US companies that export commercial goods
who_it_affects.how: Offset deals in their non-military sales abroad were set to be reviewed by the new presidential council.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies involved in trade and defense
who_it_affects.how: They would likely take part in or support the work of the new commission and council.
